channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Brasileiro é detido na Argentina em frente à embaixada antes de votar
item.description: A Brazilian citizen was arrested by Argentine police outside the Brazilian embassy in Buenos Aires before casting his vote in the 2026 elections. The arrest took place this morning, with no stated cause. The Brazilian Consulate General is following the incident.

item.title: Seleção Brasileira perderá 1º turno das eleições após amistoso na Índia
item.description: The Brazilian national football team will miss the first round of the 2026 elections due to an international friendly in India, with players departing after Saturday's match (10/3) and returning to Brazil on Monday (10/5). The flight time from Calcutta to Brazil, between 24-27 hours, prevents them from voting.

item.title: Zema com celular na cabine de votação: veja o que diz a lei e qual a pena
item.description: Presidential candidate Romeu Zema (Novo) entered the voting booth with a cell phone in Araxá, violating the rule that bans devices capable of threatening ballot secrecy. The OAB-MG noted that such conduct may constitute the crime of violating ballot secrecy, punishable by up to two years in prison. The case is under investigation by the Minas Gerais Electoral Court.

item.title: TSE afirma que 59 pessoas foram detidas por crime eleitoral
item.description: Minister of the TSE, Kassio Nunes Marques, reported that 59 people were arrested for electoral violations in the 2026 elections, including 25 in flagrante delicto. Authorities seized over R$30 million in cash since January, and the minister emphasized that the electoral process is proceeding normally, with phone confiscations at polling stations and praise for the press. He highlighted extensive preparation for the elections, reinforcing the importance of democracy.

item.title: Eleições disputadas nas urnas e nos tribunais
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian elections were marked by symmetrical suspicions surrounding all candidates and intense judicial involvement in the final stretch, creating the perception that the judiciary shifted from neutral arbiter to political actor. Contradictory court decisions, such as the suspension and reinstatement of Deltan Dallagnol's candidacy, fueled legal uncertainty and voter distrust regarding institutional impartiality. The tense atmosphere was worsened by the absence of traditional debates and single-judge TSE rulings affecting campaign dynamics.

item.title: Internautas apontam ‘sinal secreto’ de padre Marcelo Rossi em mensagem sobre as eleições
item.description: Priest Marcelo Rossi posted a video on Instagram showing his voting process but made an 'L' gesture linked to Lula's (PT) campaign, sparking speculation about his political support. The post was removed after criticism, with online users noting the coincidence of 13 files matching the PT number. The incident follows recent tensions between Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and the CNBB, which reaffirmed its trust in Our Lady of Aparecida.

item.title: TSE troca 0,16% das urnas até 12h; nenhum local precisou usar papel
item.description: Brazil's TSE reported that, by noon on election day 2026, only 935 electronic voting machines (0.16%) had been replaced, maintaining operational stability. No polling stations required manual voting, with 68,912 backup machines available. Data shows lower replacement rates in biometric locations (0.17%) versus non-biometric (0.22%).

item.title: Resultado das Eleições 2026 em Roraima: acompanhe ao vivo a apuração para senador
item.description: The vote count for senator in Roraima during the 2026 elections will be conducted live on the O GLOBO website starting at 5 PM on October 4th, with real-time updates from the TSE. The special environment will display counting progress, percentage of booths tallied, blank and null votes, and the two candidates elected to the Federal Senate. Among the candidates, Bartô Macuxi (Psol), Chico Rodrigues (PSB), and Helena da Asat are highlighted.

item.title: Não temos indicativo de interferência internacional nas eleições, diz Nunes Marques
item.description: The president of the TSE, Nunes Marques, stated there are no concrete signs of international interference in the Brazilian elections, highlighting the cooperation of big tech companies with the Electoral Justice and confidence in the electronic voting system. He also noted that challenging election results is a tradition, but hopes there will be no questions about the electoral system.

item.title: Acompanhe a apuração dos votos para presidente da República
item.description: CartaCapital's 'Direto da Redação' provides live coverage of the 2026 presidential election vote count, featuring minute-by-minute analysis and public engagement. The race is between President Lula (PT) and Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). The broadcast emphasizes factual reporting, expert opinions, and real-time updates through an interactive chat format.

item.title: Vorcaro e Stefanutto votam na Papuda; Bolsonaro não pode votar
item.description: Daniel Vorcaro and Alessandro Stefanutto voted this Sunday morning in Brasília, while Jair Bolsonaro could not vote due to being imprisoned after a definitive conviction. The first two remain under preventive detention without a final conviction, retaining their voting rights per the Constitution. Vorcaro is held at the Papudinha facility in Brasília.

item.title: MP Eleitoral pede ao TSE remoção de vídeos falsos sobre urnas e embaixadas
item.description: The Electoral Public Ministry filed two lawsuits with the TSE demanding the removal of fake videos about electronic voting machines and the closure of embassies, requesting fines for those responsible. A 2018 fake news about electoral fraud was revived on WhatsApp, while other social networks spread disinformation about terrorist threats linked to the temporary closure of US and Australian embassies.

item.title: MP Eleitoral pede retirada de conteúdos falsos sobre urnas e associação do fechamento de embaixadas a risco de golpe
item.description: The Electoral Public Ministry filed lawsuits before the TSE to demand the removal of false content about electronic voting machines and misleading information regarding the closure of embassies, linking them to risks of a coup d'état. The posts, shared by candidates and on social media, aim to misinform the electorate and generate social instability without factual basis.

item.title: Eleitores que já estiverem na fila às 17h têm direito de votar
item.description: Voters standing in line by 5 PM have the right to vote, as established by TSE norms. Ballots are distributed after identifying those waiting, and polling closes only after votes are recorded. Voting begins at 8 AM and follows Brasília time.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro vence em Israel; Lula tem maioria dos votos na Palestina
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) leads the presidential election among Brazilians in Israel with 74.29% of the votes, while Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) secures 93.09% in Palestine. Preliminary results were released before the official count by the TSE, highlighting regional voting divergences among Brazilians abroad.

item.title: Eleição no exterior: veja países em que Lula ou Flávio Bolsonaro ganharam
item.description: Poll results from New Zealand and other countries show that Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won elections in more nations, including China, Australia, Saudi Arabia, and Finland, while Flávio Bolsonaro leads in the total vote count due to Japan. The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) will release official results after 5 PM, with about 1 million Brazilian voters eligible in 186 cities across 134 countries.

item.title: Pedido de voto, celular na urna, e mais; veja infrações de candidatos durante eleição
item.description: Candidates including Flávio Bolsonaro, Lula, and Eduardo Paes were caught requesting votes after casting ballots, an electoral violation. Romeu Zema was also seen entering the voting booth with a phone, breaching election rules.

item.title: Nunes Marques diz que não há risco de interferência estrangeira nas eleições
item.description: The president of the TSE, Nunes Marques, stated that there is no risk of foreign interference in the 2026 elections, highlighting cooperation with digital platforms as a mitigating factor. He emphasized that intelligence investigations have not identified concrete threats, despite some countries issuing alerts or suspending diplomatic services before the elections.

item.title: Pode usar o celular para votar? Veja as regras nas Eleições de 2026
item.description: Candidate Romeu Zema was caught using his phone inside the voting booth in Araxá (MG), which violates electoral rules requiring devices to be handed over to the poll clerk before voting. While the e-Title app can be used for identification, phones must not be used during the actual vote to protect ballot secrecy. The case is under investigation by the Electoral Court.

item.title: Apuração Eleições 2026: tudo que você precisa saber
item.description: The 2026 general elections will take place on October 4th, featuring voting for president, governors, senators, and federal and state deputies. Real-time results will be available on g1 using TSE data. Voters can check their polling zone and section via the TSE's online self-service or the e-Título app.

item.title: Flávio pede 'voto de confiança', e Lula cita número de urna; juristas se dividem se declarações configuram crime eleitoral
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro asked for a vote of confidence in a statement after voting, while Lula cited his ballot number; legal experts are divided on whether these statements constitute an electoral crime.

item.title: Quem estiver na fila às 17h ainda pode votar? O que diz o TSE
item.description: Voters standing in line by 5 PM will be allowed to cast their ballots, as per the TSE guidelines. Polls are open from 8 AM to 5 PM and cover president, governor, two senators, and federal and state deputies. Senate votes are nominal and restricted to candidates from the voter’s state.

item.title: ASSISTA: g1 faz cobertura especial do primeiro turno das eleições
item.description: The 2026 elections reach the final stretch with special coverage of the first round on g1. Voting takes place until 5 PM Brasília time, with regional adjustments. Voters need an official ID with photo and must follow the voting order for positions.

item.title: Flávio vence em Israel, Lula ganha na Palestina
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) won the election among Brazilian voters in Israel with 74.40% of valid votes, while Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) secured 13.09%. In Palestine, Lula led with 93.09% of the votes, surpassing Flávio who received 3.97%.

item.title: Sistema eleitoral opera em total normalidade, diz Nunes Marques
item.description: The president of the TSE, Kassio Nunes Marques, stated that the Brazilian electoral system operates with full transparency and normality, rejecting criticisms of the electoral process. He emphasized the efficiency of Electoral Justice in ensuring access to voting sections, particularly in the Northern Region, and the replacement of voting machines with technical failures, which will be properly counted. Nunes Marques also commented on the prohibition of cell phones in voting booths, the suspension of consular activities abroad, and the ineffectiveness of misinformation in changing election results.

item.title: Boletim de Urna permite conferir totalização dos votos; entenda
item.description: Starting at 5 PM this Sunday (4), any voter can act as an election observer by checking the Boletim de Urna, a printed report generated by each electronic voting machine containing vote counts and a QR code. Voters can scan the QR codes using the official Boletim na Mão or e-Título app and compare the data with official results published by the TSE at resultados.tse.jus.br, ensuring transparency in vote tallying. According to Michel Kovacs, Information Technology Secretary at TRE-RJ, this process, in use since 2008, has never shown discrepancies.

item.title: TSE substitui 0,2% das urnas e diz não ver sinal de interferência estrangeira na eleição
item.description: The TSE reported that 0.2% of voting machines were replaced due to power fluctuations, mainly in Paraná, and detected no signs of foreign interference in the election. The TSE president emphasized the transparency of the process and the absence of relevant deepfakes on social media.

item.title: PF diz que apura possibilidade de intervenção externa sobre eleições; TSE não vê ‘indício concreto’
item.description: The Federal Police opened a procedure to investigate possible external interference in elections, following a request from the AGU. The TSE president stated there are no concrete signs of international interference in the election. The embassies of the United States and Australia closed their doors due to security concerns, but the PF found no effective risks to diplomatic representations.

item.title: Eleições 2026 AO VIVO: Acompanhe a votação para Presidente no 1º turno
item.description: The 2026 first-round presidential election in Brazil is underway, also deciding governors, senators, and federal deputies. Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro lead the polls, followed by Augusto Cury, Renan Santos, and Caiado.

item.title: Moro vota em Curitiba, celebra decisão do TSE sobre Deltan e defende campanha limpa
item.description: Sérgio Moro, a PL candidate for Governor of Paraná, voted this Sunday in Curitiba and celebrated the TSE ruling that secured Deltan Dallagnol's eligibility. The former judge advocated for a clean campaign and reaffirmed his anti-corruption stance following the favorable verdict.

item.title: Augusto Cury (Avante) vota em Colina, interior de São Paulo
item.description: Presidential candidate Augusto Cury (Avante) cast his vote in Colina, an inland city in São Paulo state, around 11 a.m. this Sunday, the 4th. He is running for the Planalto Palace on a ticket with Júlio Delgado, also from Avante.

item.title: Tarcísio: 'tenho visto migração de outros candidatos para Flávio Bolsonaro, estou otimista'
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas, running for reelection, stated that he sees a migration of voters from other right-wing candidates in support of Flávio Bolsonaro and expressed optimism about the electoral scenario. He emphasized the current movement of consolidating the conservative base for the 2026 elections.

item.title: TSE: 55 auditores do TCU acompanham teste de integridade no Brasil; não há intercorrências
item.description: The TSE reported that 421 voting machines were replaced and 55 TCU auditors are monitoring the integrity test without incidents.

item.title: Brasileiros votam na Itália: eleitorado cresce em 2026, mas índice de abstenção é alto
item.description: Brazilians in Italy prepare for 2026 voting with increased participation, but face high abstention rates. In Rome, Piazza Navona divides between political groups, reflecting polarization of the Brazilian electorate abroad. The atmosphere mixes celebration with tension between different ideological orientations.

item.title: Renan Santos vota em SP, diz que eleição foi vazia e chama Flávio Bolsonaro de ‘desqualificado, covarde e burro’
item.description: Renan Santos, federal congressman elected from São Paulo, publicly criticized the 2026 election as 'meaningless' and launched a scathing personal attack on Senator Flávio Bolsonaro, calling him 'disqualified, cowardly, and stupid.' His remarks sparked mixed reactions in the political arena, with condemnations over disrespect and defenses citing freedom of speech.

item.title: Renan Santos vota em SP e diz que eleição é ‘a mais bizarra de todas’
item.description: Candidate Renan Santos (Missão) voted in São Paulo and harshly criticized the election, calling it 'the strangest ever', arguing that no proposals were discussed and major political forces are embroiled in corruption scandals.

item.title: Brasileiro tem o direito de sonhar, diz Cury ao votar
item.description: Augusto Cury, Avante's presidential candidate, voted in Colina (SP) and emphasized the vote as a transformative tool, stating: 'Neither steak nor rifle, Augusto Cury to change Brazil'. A recent poll shows Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro tied with 46% of voting intentions for a potential second round, while Cury has 3% in the first round.

item.title: Elecciones en Brasil 2026, en vivo | Lula y Bolsonaro votan en la primera vuelta por la presidencia
item.description: Brazil holds one of its most competitive presidential elections, with Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva seeking reelection and Flávio Bolsonaro, son of Jair Bolsonaro, running on the right. Lula expressed confidence in victory, while Bolsonaro claimed the country needs change. This first round will determine who advances to a potential runoff.

item.title: Haddad diz que fez “grande campanha” e sai “com espírito leve”
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) stated after voting in the 2026 municipal elections that he ran a 'great campaign' and leaves with a light spirit, highlighting the climate of dialogue and openness among São Paulo voters. He thanked voters and noted the atmosphere is better than in 2022.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro fala em 'voto de revolta'; Lula aposta em 'dia glorioso'; veja como foi a manhã dos candidatos
item.description: Presidential candidates Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) and Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) cast their ballots Sunday morning, highlighting the electoral uncertainty shown in recent polls. Both remain statistically tied in the latest surveys ahead of the 2026 first-round vote.

item.title: Presidente do STF, Edson Fachin vota no 1º turno das Eleições 2026
item.description: The President of the Supreme Federal Court (STF), Minister Edson Fachin, voted in the first round of the 2026 elections in Brasília, emphasizing the importance of voting as an expression of popular sovereignty and highlighting the role of the Electoral Justice in ensuring a transparent election.

item.title: Eleições no RJ: principais candidatos ao governo do estado já votaram
item.description: Voters in Rio de Janeiro cast their ballots on Sunday (4) in municipal and state elections, choosing candidates for federal deputy, state deputy, two Senate seats, governor, and president. Voting takes place from 8 a.m. to 5 p.m. Brasília time, and a voter ID card is not required—only an official photo ID.

item.title: Fachin vota em Brasília
item.description: The President of the Supreme Federal Court (STF) and National Justice Council (CNJ), Luiz Edson Fachin, voted in Brasília on Sunday. He attended the Centro de Ensino Fundamental 214 Sul in the Asa Sul district, waited in line and spoke with voters. Fachin stated he will address the press after completing his vote, emphasizing the importance of conscious voting.

item.title: Tarcísio de Freitas vota e prega humildade na espera pelo resultado
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas voted in the first round of the São Paulo elections and called for humility while awaiting the count, expressing optimism and highlighting the support received during the campaign.

item.title: Meia da seleção australiana, Irvine demonstra apoio a Lula nas redes
item.description: Australian national team player Jackson Irvine expressed support for Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) on social media by featuring the candidate's number 13 in posts on election Sunday. He also paid tribute to Sócrates, former Corinthians player associated with the Democracia Corintiana movement. Irvine, currently playing for Cerezo Osaka, is a key figure in Australia's national squad.

item.title: Quantas urnas precisaram ser trocadas pelo TSE por falhas técnicas na manhã do primeiro turno
item.description: The TSE reported that 421 electronic voting machines were replaced by 10 AM on election day due to technical failures, representing 0.07% of all equipment in use. São Paulo leads replacement occurrences with 86 cases, followed by Paraná with 60. The Electoral Justice maintains contingency machines and technical teams monitoring equipment security with no irregularities recorded.

item.title: Haddad vota acompanhado de Alckmin, Marina e Tebet: ‘saindo com espírito leve’
item.description: Fernando Haddad (PT) voted accompanied by Alckmin, Marina, Tebet, and Márcio França, highlighting the dialogue atmosphere of the campaign. He thanked voters and expressed satisfaction, emphasizing the light spirit of the campaign. Before voting, he had breakfast with Lula, whom he described as being in good spirits.

item.title: Eleições 2026: acompanhe a apuração em todo o Brasil pelo g1
item.description: The 2026 Brazilian elections, held on October 4, elected governors, senators, federal and state deputies, and the president. Results were streamed live by G1 using TSE data, featuring interactive maps and zone-level vote tracking. Voters could access detailed results, including votes per municipality and polling booth, enhancing electoral transparency.

item.title: Zema descumpre regra e usa celular na cabine de votação
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo presidential candidate, was caught entering the voting booth in Araxá (MG) with two cell phones, violating electoral rules. Press footage captured the moment, and the case was referred to the TRE-MG, where officials deemed the behavior irregular and potentially punishable. Zema denied recording or photographing his vote, claiming he was not warned by poll workers about the restriction.

item.title: Renan Santos vota em SP e dispara contra Flávio: “Covarde e burro”
item.description: Renan Santos, a presidential candidate from the Missão party, voted in São Paulo's southern zone and launched attacks against Flávio Bolsonaro, calling him 'cowardly and stupid' and questioning his performance and voter support.
